title: Rust walls and facades: windows as recessed openings with sills, seams breaking the slab
note: Windows are openings with a reveal ≥ 0.1 m, a sill and set-back glazing; seams and a plinth break every large wall.
intent: Flat walls with windows painted on score generic every time, inside and out. Build a window as an opening: the wall stops around it, four returns of the wall's material make a reveal at least 0.1 m deep, a sill sticks out below, and the glazing (or the grille and the blown-out daylight behind it) sits at the back of the reveal. The best answer is a wall kit from Local Blender (walls with openings, frames, sills, radiators, skirting, with world-scale UVs) drawn as models; with the facade's primitives, draw the reveal from cubes as in the sketch and keep it on the same panel grid as the wall. Break every large plane: seam or skirting lines, a darker plinth or dado band, a cornice; no run of four identical bays without an interruption. Light an opening with a spot shining in and an emissive pane (Material::emissive), not a white box.

check.ask: Are the windows set back into the wall with a visible depth (a reveal and a sill), and do lines or bands break up the large wall surfaces?
check.note: Windows recessed ≥ 0.1 m with sills, seams and bands breaking the slab; flat walls with painted windows score generic every time.

port: The level facet owns walls and openings (or the kit models); a light facet owns the spot behind each window.

evidence.note: frame.cube_with and frame.model; models of 512+ triangles get levels at import.
The three.js recipe facade.recessed-windows-seams, ported to the genex facade (bodycam B4).
